content.content:
Discarding is the end of an open draft, and that end — without landing, outside the operation vocabulary, with a drifted draft still an open draft — is settled by tvxspkyy; what that end leaves open is the change-side question this node answers: which change a discard makes go away. The answer is the change the draft's workspace holds. Opening a draft created its workspace at the change that owns the draft's node, so the workspace's working copy holds the node's owned set as the record's base records it (pvnszwum). The working copy is therefore a change of its own whose parent is the node's owning change: the workspace's start is the node's change, and the change the workspace holds is the working-copy change one step above that start. The two are distinct, and the ids keep them distinct: a node's id is the id of the jj change that owns the node, and the draft's working-copy change is not a node (xwyryumr). The node id therefore names the parent of the change in question, never the change itself.

The act is abandonment. A change is removed by abandoning it with `jj abandon` (xllzxxvo), so discarding abandons the working-copy change the workspace holds, and nothing else is that abandonment's object. The object is not selected by node id, which names the parent (xwyryumr), and not by matching the draft's content against candidate changes, because opening fixed the workspace at the one change that owns the node and the working copy is the change above that start (pvnszwum). The act is abandonment — `jj abandon` — and not another act wearing its name (xllzxxvo). Which invocation and which flags carry the abandonment are not fixed here.

One change goes away, and no other goes with it. The draft never landed, so what the working copy holds is unlanded work and nothing of it was ever recorded into the node's change (tvxspkyy); abandoning it leaves the node's owned set as the base records it, so the node's owning change is not touched (pvnszwum, tvxspkyy). That change stays exactly what it was — the change the node's id names (xwyryumr) and the parent the workspace started from (pvnszwum) — and it is not the abandonment's object. Every other change is untouched for the same reason: abandoning is per change (xllzxxvo), the abandonment names the one change the workspace holds, and nothing selects a second change as its object, so no other change is abandoned with it or in its place. The changes that carry other nodes, and the changes of other drafts, are not reached.

When the workspace is already gone, the end is still a discard — a drifted draft is still an open draft, and discarding it is not a repair of drift (tvxspkyy) — but the change it would abandon is the one the workspace holds, and the workspace is the only place the start is read from (pvnszwum). The record then reaches no change: there is no working-copy change at a start that no longer exists, and no substitute is taken for it — not the node's owning change, which the node id names and which is the parent (xwyryumr, pvnszwum), and not a change found by searching, matched by content, or invented for the occasion. So nothing is abandoned, and jj's state is left exactly as it stands. What the record then does is another commitment's to say; this node settles only that the change-side act reaches nothing.

The change it abandons is the draft's working-copy change, not a node's, so the abandonment is not a graph operation: the discard remains the end of a draft rather than a removal in the operation vocabulary (tvxspkyy, xwyryumr). The change is the draft's own, unlanded working-copy change, and it carries no node.

These clauses are one commitment, not several: one change, one act, one exclusion, one empty case. Which change a discard makes go away has one answer — the working-copy change the draft's workspace holds — and each clause is that answer read where it could be mistaken: read at the node's id, where the answer must not become the node's change (xwyryumr); read at the node's change, where the answer must not take the parent with it (pvnszwum); read at a missing workspace, where the answer must not invent or substitute a change (tvxspkyy); and read at the act, where the answer must be abandonment and not a second removal mechanism (xllzxxvo). Take any clause away and the answer is a different one: drop the object and the act has nothing to abandon; drop the exclusion and the node's change goes with the draft's; drop the empty case and the record reaches a change jj no longer holds; drop the act and removal has two mechanisms. The clauses hold together or not at all.

Deliberately not here. The record's removal from the store — the document, its path, the scan and the retention — is another commitment, relied on and not restated; so are the forgetting or removal of the discarded draft's workspace and its directory; the verb surface (the command, its name, flags, arguments, output, refusal wording and exit status); and the exact jj invocation and flags by which the abandonment is carried out. This node fixes only which change a discard abandons, and that it abandons no other.
content.rationale:
This node is prose because the commitment is which change a discard makes go away, and every prerequisite that grounds it is prose; each of the four edges is a natural-to-natural reading, answered by reading the clauses against the recorded decisions rather than by any behavior probe.

The node takes the discard as tvxspkyy settles it — the end of an open draft, without landing, outside the operation vocabulary — and answers only the change-side question that end leaves open. Opening puts a draft's workspace at the change that owns the node (pvnszwum), so the workspace's working copy is a change whose parent is the node's owning change; xwyryumr says a node's id names that owning change and that the working-copy change is not a node, so the change to abandon is the working-copy change, selected from the workspace's start and never from the node's id. xllzxxvo fixes the act as abandonment with jj abandon, so this node names the act without fixing the invocation or the flags, which belong to the implementation layer.

Each prerequisite carries an element and each element names its prerequisite: pvnszwum carries the workspace-start identification of the change and the exclusion of the parent from the object; xwyryumr carries the id distinction that keeps the node's change out of the object and the non-node standing of the working-copy change; xllzxxvo carries the act and its per-change scope; tvxspkyy carries the drifted-draft case, in which the record reaches no change and jj is left alone, together with the fact that the draft never landed, so the node's owned set is untouched.

Deliberately not here, because each can be decided, changed or dropped without touching which change is abandoned: the record's removal from the store; the forgetting or removal of the workspace and its directory; the verb surface; and the exact invocation and flags. This node fixes one answer — the change the draft's workspace holds — and that no other change is abandoned with it.
